name: Nose contouring makeup
lead: Nose contouring is a makeup technique in which a darker shade is applied along the sides of the nose and a lighter shade on the bridge or tip, with the aim of making the nose look slimmer, straighter or more defined through light and shadow. It is a specific application of contouring, defined as using cosmetics to define, enhance and sculpt facial structure.[1]

The look rests on a simple optical principle: darker shades create shadow and a slimming effect, while lighter shades bring forward areas that are more prominent.[1] Placing a shade one or two tones darker beside the nose and a lighter one on the tip or bridge is meant to make the nose read as narrower and straighter in person and in photos.[1]

The practice changes only the visual impression of the nose while the makeup is worn and does not alter its structure. It is widely discussed alongside non-surgical and surgical nose changes as the lowest-commitment option, and is used both in everyday makeup and in stage, film and drag makeup.[1]
infobox: Powder or cream contour and highlight shades[1]

paras: In general contouring, a shade one or two tones darker than the skin is placed in hollows such as along the sides of the nose, cheeks and temples to create shadow, and a lighter shade is placed on more prominent areas such as the tip of the nose to draw light.[1] Powder palettes with light and dark shades and cream products are commonly used.[1] Strobing is a related approach that uses lighter shades only.[1]

Powder contour, often sold in palettes with light and dark shades, gives a softer result, while cream contour can give a more emphasized look.[1] Contour shades can be warm or cool, and are chosen relative to the wearer's skin tone.[1]

Shading the face with makeup has theatrical roots: Elizabethan stage actors reportedly used chalk and soot, and greasepaint replaced soot after electric stage lighting arrived in the late 1800s.[1] Max Factor Sr. added shading to film makeup in 1934 and presented a contouring tutorial for different face shapes in 1945.[1] Makeup artist Kevyn Aucoin's 2000 book Face Forward is credited with introducing contouring to the general public, and celebrities such as Kim Kardashian are credited with popularizing it further in the 2010s as brands began selling dedicated contour products.[1] Film star Marlene Dietrich is reported to have contoured her own face in the 1920s and 1930s, and subtle contouring was used by actresses of the 1950s such as Audrey Hepburn, Marilyn Monroe and Elizabeth Taylor.[1] Drag performers use contouring to emphasize or soften features.[1]
No studies found. Published research that appears in searches for related terms concerns surgical nasal reconstruction and nasal anatomy rather than the effect of makeup on perceived nose shape.

Within appearance communities, nose contouring is generally described as a reversible, non-surgical way to alter perceived nose width or straightness, often compared with nose taping, fillers and rhinoplasty. Specific community claims about it are not documented in the sources reviewed.

card.summary: Shading and highlighting to make the nose look slimmer; purely optical, reversible and untested in studies.
card.note: Temporary visual effect only; no studies of its perceived effect were found.

quick.overview:
Nose contouring uses a darker shade on the sides of the nose and a lighter one on the bridge or tip to create the illusion of a slimmer, straighter nose.

It is an established makeup technique with roots in theatre and film, popularized more widely in the 2010s.
quick.mechanism: Dark shades recede and light shades advance visually, so shading along the sides of the nose can make it look narrower. Nothing about the underlying structure changes.
quick.risks: Risks are those of ordinary cosmetics, such as skin irritation or breakouts in sensitive individuals. The effect disappears when the makeup is removed.

chain: Darker shade applied along sides of the nose
Lighter shade placed on bridge or tip
Shadow and highlight change how light reads on the nose
Nose appears slimmer and straighter while worn
angle.text: Nose contouring changes the look of the nose right away with powder or cream makeup and washes off at the end of the day. People use it for events, photos and everyday makeup when they want a slimmer or straighter-looking nose without any procedure.
